# Ways of playing

<!-- GENERATED by src/dsp/factory/__tests__/ways-doc.test.ts from the table in src/dsp/factory/ways. Do not edit. -->

The ways a sound can be played (`WAYS`), family by family in the order a
host lists them. What a way is, what a take keeps and how takes are counted
is in [factory.md](./factory.md#a-way-of-playing-a-sound). The last column
is where `far` stands when a host names none.

## One at a time

| Way id           | Name           | What it needs                              | What it does                                                                                                                                                        | What `far` changes                                 | `far` |
| ---------------- | -------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- | ----- |
| `rising`         | Rising         | A held chord, or a phrase of three pitches | The notes of the chord one after another, low to high. Each turn starts one note further up. The note the sound stands on stays where it is.                        | Past half, the notes run on into the octave above. | 0.25  |
| `there-and-back` | There and back | A held chord, or a phrase of three pitches | Up through the chord and down again, carried on from where the last turn stopped. The note the sound stands on stays where it is.                                   | Past half, the notes run on into the octave above. | 0.25  |
| `outside-in`     | Outside in     | A held chord, or a phrase of three pitches | The lowest note of the chord, then the highest, then inwards from both ends. Each turn starts one place further on. The note the sound stands on stays where it is. | Past half, the notes run on into the octave above. | 0.25  |
| `carry-on`       | Carry on       | A phrase of three single notes             | The phrase reads its own notes with the last left off, and carries on from turn to turn, so the same rhythm plays a line that comes round a note later each time.   | Past half, two notes are left off.                 | 0.25  |

## Counting

| Way id           | Name           | What it needs                       | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | What `far` changes                                                     | `far` |
| ---------------- | -------------- | ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----- |
| `counted-rests`  | Counted rests  | A phrase or a beat                  | Each moment of the phrase has a count of 1, 2, 3 or 2, by its place. It sounds on every turn its count divides and rests on the others, so the first turn is the phrase as written and it all comes round after six. The first moment and the note the sound stands on always sound. | How many of the moments count. The others sound on every turn.         | 0.5   |
| `leave-one-out`  | Leave one out  | A phrase or a beat                  | One moment of the phrase rests each turn, the next one along each time. In a long phrase eight moments take their turn, spread through it. The first moment and the note the sound stands on always sound.                                                                           | Past half, two moments rest each turn.                                 | 0.25  |
| `turning-rests`  | Turning rests  | A phrase or a beat                  | Rests spread as evenly through the phrase as they go, and the whole spread moves on a place each turn, or a few places in a long phrase. The first moment and the note the sound stands on always sound.                                                                             | The share of the moments that rests, up to two in five.                | 0.5   |
| `sliding-window` | Sliding window | A phrase or a beat of eight moments | A window of the phrase sounds and what is outside it rests. The window moves on by a quarter of the phrase each turn and comes round after four. The first moment and the note the sound stands on always sound.                                                                     | The size of the window: a quarter of the phrase, up to three quarters. | 0.5   |

## Growth

| Way id           | Name           | What it needs             | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                               | What `far` changes                                                         | `far` |
| ---------------- | -------------- | ------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----- |
| `gather`         | Gather         | A phrase or a beat        | A quarter of the phrase's moments, then half, then three quarters, then all of it, one step a turn. The first moment always sounds, and so does every moment that holds the note the sound stands on.      | Where it starts: a quarter of the phrase, or past half one moment.         | 0.25  |
| `one-note-slips` | One note slips | A phrase of three pitches | Each turn one more note has moved to its neighbour in the key, and stays there on the turns after. After four the phrase is as written again. The first note and the note the sound stands on never move.  | How far a note slips: a step, or past half a third.                        | 0.25  |
| `climb`          | Climb          | A phrase of three pitches | Every note above the note the sound stands on sits one note of the chord higher each turn, from the top of the chord round to the bottom, and comes home after four turns.                                 | How many turns before it comes home: two, three or, at its furthest, four. | 1     |
| `lean`           | Lean           | A phrase of three pitches | Each note is played one moment later and one note of the chord higher each turn, so the line leans across its own rhythm. The moments keep their times, lengths and touch. It comes home after four turns. | How many turns before it comes home: two, three or, at its furthest, four. | 1     |

## Trades

| Way id            | Name            | What it needs                 | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | What `far` changes                                         | `far` |
| ----------------- | --------------- | ----------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | ----- |
| `neighbours-swap` | Neighbours swap | A phrase of four single notes | Neighbouring notes of the phrase change places each turn, one set of pairs and then the other, so the notes walk through each other. Each turn builds on the last. The first note of the phrase and the note the sound stands on stay where they are. | How many turns before it comes home: four to eight.        | 0.5   |
| `home-and-away`   | Home and away   | A phrase of three pitches     | Three turns as written, then one upside down within its own chord: a note that is so far from the bottom of the chord plays the note that far from the top. The rhythm and the note the sound stands on stay.                                         | Past half, one turn at home for each turn away, not three. | 0.25  |

## Held

| Way id               | Name               | What it needs               | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | What `far` changes                     | `far` |
| -------------------- | ------------------ | --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ----- |
| `staggered-entries`  | Staggered entries  | A held chord of three notes | The note the chord stands on holds, and the notes above it come in one at a time through the pass, each held from where it enters. The order they enter in moves round by one each turn.                                                          | How much of the pass the entries take. | 0.5   |
| `voices-come-and-go` | Voices come and go | A held chord of three notes | One note above the one the chord stands on leaves part way through the pass, and the note that left last turn comes back as it goes. The rest hold. The top note leaves first, then the next one down.                                            | When in the pass they trade.           | 0.5   |
| `unequal-rounds`     | Unequal rounds     | A held chord of three notes | Each note above the one the chord stands on is struck again at a count of its own, the top note the shortest, and no two counts have a factor in common. The counts carry on from turn to turn, so the notes fall together differently each time. | How fine the grid they count on is.    | 0.25  |

## Hits and voices

| Way id        | Name        | What it needs             | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                             | What `far` changes                                                                                | `far` |
| ------------- | ----------- | ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----- |
| `echoes`      | Echoes      | One hit that ends         | One to three softer repeats of the hit after it, at its own pitch, each softer than the one before. How many there are and how far apart they come changes every turn. The hit itself stays as it is.                    | How many repeats there may be, one to three, and how late the last may come.                      | 0.5   |
| `two-readers` | Two readers | A phrase of three pitches | A second, softer voice joins every third moment of the phrase. It reads the notes of the phrase in order, a fifth higher in the key, and carries on each turn from where it stopped. The written notes stay as they are. | How soft the second voice is: the further, the less soft, and never as hard as the note it joins. | 0.5   |
| `in-the-gaps` | In the gaps | A phrase with rests       | The phrase stays as written. A note of its chord sounds in one of its widest gaps, a different gap each turn.                                                                                                            | Past half, two gaps are filled each turn.                                                         | 0.25  |
